description: Ca₉MgNa(PO₄)₇ crystallizes in the trigonal R3c space group. Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are three shorter (2.43 Å) and three longer (2.84 Å) Na-O bond lengths. There are three inequivalent Ca sites. In the first Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.40-2.65 Å. In the second Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.38-2.71 Å. In the third Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.84 Å. Mg is bonded to six O atoms to form MgO₆ octahedra that share corners with six PO₄ tetrahedra. There are three shorter (2.09 Å) and three longer (2.11 Å) Mg-O bond lengths. There are three inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 51°. There are three shorter (1.55 Å) and one longer (1.56 Å) P-O bond length. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 42°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.55-1.58 Å. In the third P site, P is bonded in a tetrahedral geometry to four O atoms. There is one shorter (1.55 Å) and three longer (1.56 Å) P-O bond lengths. There are ten inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to three Ca and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Ca, one Mg, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Ca and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Ca and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted tetrahedral geometry to three equivalent Ca and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Ca, one Mg, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ca, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Ca and one P atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ca, and one P atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Ca and one P atom.
